focus: Stress-test the accent and subgraph rows and fit new rules into the checker self-test
noveltyJustification: All findings are synthesis or implementation analysis of the target file; two verdicts are reversed or narrowed, and (2 + 0.5*10) / 12 = 0.583, discounted to 0.52 for two restatements.
keyQuestions: Which layout, colour, shape, density and label limits does the corpus treat as enforceable versus advisory, and do they support or contradict Flow Mode's limits (TD only, 9 nodes, 3 decision exits, one accent colour, four shapes)?

label: Accent family is not implementable without a palette, so iteration 10's recommendation is withdrawn and the check stays at one hex.
One hex remains the right unit for a nine-node flow because colour marks one thing and the model has no note or warning role vocabulary.
Subgraph verdict: reject explicitly, because the nine-node cap makes grouping low value and the official recipe needs per-subgraph tints.
Supporting subgraphs would cascade into three rule changes: tinted fills, per-subgraph direction and node-to-node edges.
The four mechanical checks fit the checker's existing shape as a constant plus a condition in diagram_problems, with no new dependency.
The subgraph check must read block_text like the accent check, because the extractor drops styling and grouping structure.
The reserved-ID check needs whole-word, case-insensitive matching so ending and weekend do not trip end.
The emoji check should scan labels and edge labels through one helper, matching the existing MARKUP_MARKS coverage.
Label length should be a hard error at 80 characters after trimming, since 120 is too loose for a board at this size.
Every new rule needs its own planted model: emoji label, reserved-ID node, underscore ID, 81-character label and a subgraph block.
The existing GOOD fixture survives all five additions because it uses short labels, camelCase IDs, one accent and four nodes.
The underscore rule must apply to node IDs only, since Flow Mode edges carry prose labels and no identifiers.

reason: No palette or family membership rule exists, so the check would be arbitrary and untestable.
